question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the roots of $g(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-16}{{x}^{2}-7x+10}$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}$\,$
and

$\,x=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The roots of $g(x)$ are the solutions to the equation $g(x)=0.$ In our case, we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-16}{{x}^{2}-7x+10}=0.
$$

First, we factor $g(x),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(x) & =\frac{{x}^{2}-16}{{x}^{2}-7x+10} \\  & =\frac{(x+4)(x-4)}{(x-2)(x-5)}\end{aligned}
$$

There are no common factors in the numerator and denominator, so we set the numerator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+4)(x-4) & =0 \\ x & =-4,\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions to $g(x)=0$, in ascending order, are $x=-4$ and $x=4.$
